nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiMoO4 synthesis
nodes.procedure: 2 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 2 mmol Na2MoO4·2H2O, and 35 mL of H2O were mixed to form a clear solution. The mixture was transferred into a Teflon-lined stainless autoclave (50 mL) and heated at 150°C for 6 h. After reaction, NiMoO4 powder was obtained by centrifugation, which was then washed and dried for use.

nodes.name: PBA-0 synthesis
nodes.procedure: 40 mg of NiMoO4 powder was dispersed in the 20 mL K4Fe(CN)6·3H2O (0.3 mmol) aqueous solution with ultrasonication. After 2 h of reaction with drastic stirring at room temperature, the product was centrifuged, washed, and dried to obtain PBA-0.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM image of PBA-60 reveals rod-like structure with jagged edges consisting of interconnected, welded cubes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a shows the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image of the PBA bombarded with N2 plasma for 60 min (which we abbreviate PBA-60), revealing the rod-like structure with jagged edges.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM image of PBA-60 displays crystalline domains with discontinuous atomic arrangement and peak valleys in atomic intensity profile, suggesting presence of V_CN.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2b gives a high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image of PBA-60, which displays crystalline domains with discontinuous atomic arrangement, as further demonstrated by the peak valleys of the atomic intensity profile (inset in Fig. 2b).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD analysis uncovers the cubic K2NiFe(CN)6 phase of the pristine PBA with no noticeable phase changes after N2 plasma bombardment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis uncovers the cubic K2NiFe(CN)6 phase of the pristine PBA (JCPDS 20-0915; Supplementary Fig. 4).

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area of PBA-60 is 68.3 m² g⁻¹, larger than pristine PBAs due to more accessible vacancy sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area of the PBA-60 was determined to be 68.3 m² g⁻¹, larger than the value of pristine PBAs (i.e., PBA-0) owing to the more accessible vacancy sites.

nodes.characterization_summary: PAS shows positron lifetime τ₁ of 267 ps for PBA-60 matching calculated 270 ps for V_CN, confirming positron annihilation at CN vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The measured shorter component (τ₁) of 267 ps for PBA-60 matches well with the calculated positron lifetime of 270 ps for V_CN, implying that positron annihilation traps at such vacancies.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES shows bulk V_CN contents of ~3.2, 4.5, 7.5, and 11.4% for PBA-10, PBA-30, PBA-60, and PBA-120 respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The bulk V_CN contents of ~3.2, 4.5, 7.5, and 11.4% are determined for PBA-10, PBA-30, PBA-60, and PBA-120.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge EXAFS shows Ni–N coordination number decreases from 5.9 to 5.5; Fe K-edge shows Fe–C coordination number decreases from 6.1 to 5.7 for PBA-60.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Our Ni and Fe K-edge extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) fittings reveal that... the first-shell Ni–N coordination number decreases from 5.9 to 5.5 and the Fe–C coordination number decreases from 6.1 to 5.7.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra of PBA-60 shows disappearance of 2225 cm⁻¹ peak corresponding to FeIII-CN-NiII, indicating changed oxidation state of FeIII species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We found that the peak at 2225 cm⁻¹ disappears for PBA-60 sample, meaning the changed oxidation state of FeIII species.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni L3-edge and Fe L3-edge XAS spectra show Ni L3-edge shoulder peak shift from 855.1 eV to 855.6 eV indicating surface Ni2+ partially oxidized to Ni3+; Fe L3-edge shows increased intensity of left peak indicating lowered Fe oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As Fig. 4d shows, the Ni L3-edge shoulder peak shifts from 855.1 eV (PBA-0) to 855.6 eV (PBA-60), indicating that surface Ni2+ ions were partially oxidized to Ni3+ after N2 plasma bombardment. The Fe L3-edge XAS spectra in Fig. 4e... reveal... The increased intensity of the left peak demonstrates lowered oxidation state of Fe with the formation of V_CN.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms decreased N/Ni and C/Fe atomic ratios with plasma treatment time and oxidation state changes consistent with XAS; surface V_CN contents slightly higher than bulk.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We applied... ICP-AES... and elemental analysis... whereas the surface component evolution was determined by the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). We found that... the atomic ratios of N/Ni and C/Fe decreased with time... The above oxidation-state analyses match well with our XPS studies presented in Supplementary Fig. 27.

nodes.characterization_summary: ESR shows signal at g-factor=2.03 appearing after 10 min bombardment, dominant at 60 min, originating from unpaired electrons of Ni3+ species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ESR measurements show that an ESR signal appears at g-factor=2.03 just after 10 min of bombardment, which becomes dominant when bombarding for 60 min.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM elemental mapping shows no clear C and N fades throughout PBA-60 nanorods, indicating V_CN concentration does not notably alter bulk components.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning TEM (STEM) elemental mapping shows no clear C and N fades throughout the PBA-60 nanorods (Fig. 2c), which reveals that the concentration of V_CN does not notably alter the bulk components.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX analyses show Fe suffers certain loss at first 5 h of cycling for PBA-60 then retained up to 25 h; PBA-0 loses most Fe after 25 h operation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) analyses reveal that Fe suffers a certain loss at the first 5 h of cycling for PBA-60, which is retained thereafter even up to 25 h... In contrast, the PBA-0 loses most Fe in the structure after 25 h of continuous operation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Time-dependent FT-IR spectra of PBA-60 show bands at 3650 cm⁻¹, 880 cm⁻¹, and 640 cm⁻¹ becoming dominant, belonging to O–H stretching in brucite-like Ni(OH)2, Fe–O–H, and Ni–O–H bending modes indicating Ni–Fe oxy(hydroxide) formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The time-dependent Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectra on PBA-60 catalyst exhibit that three bands at 3650 cm⁻¹, 880 cm⁻¹, and 640 cm⁻¹ become dominant with time... indicating the formation of Ni–Fe oxy (hydroxide) active surface layer during OER.
